question: Should OpenClaw add one global operational-reply policy with persistent once-state and operator-session redirect, and which redirect-persistence failure contract should it guarantee?
rationale: This choice creates a user-facing configuration surface, changes which runtime information reaches external recipients, and sets a security-sensitive failure mode that cannot be selected safely from implementation evidence alone.

options.title: Approve a narrow fail-closed policy
options.body: Keep `always` as the compatibility default, permit explicit silent/once/redirect modes, and preserve source suppression when redirect persistence fails.

options.title: Require retry semantics first
options.body: Do not merge redirect mode until an operator-session retry and observability contract is specified and proven without source-chat fallback.

options.title: Reduce scope to source suppression
options.body: Land only the established fallback-leak fix and defer global once/redirect policy design to a separate approved proposal.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow fail-closed policy
recommendation.body: Keep `always` as the compatibility default, permit explicit silent/once/redirect modes, and preserve source suppression when redirect persistence fails.

likelyOwner.reason: The linked implementation proposal is the concrete current design artifact, though an authorized product and security owner must make the final decision.
